title: When a tulip cost as much as a house

scenes.say: Would you swap a HOUSE for a flower? In sixteen thirty seven, in the Netherlands, some people basically did! This is tulip mania!

Rare striped tulips were the ultimate flex. Funny thing? The stripes were caused by a virus! One famous bulb, the Semper Augustus, was reportedly valued at around ten thousand guilders. Enough for a fancy house in Amsterdam!
For comparison, Rembrandt got about sixteen hundred guilders for his most famous painting. A flower beat the Night Watch!
But here's the twist. People weren't even trading flowers! They traded promises to buy bulbs later, in pubs, flipping them again and again for higher prices!
Then in February sixteen thirty seven, at an auction in Haarlem... nobody bought. Prices crashed in days! Oops!

Fun fact: historians now say it didn't actually ruin the country. A lot of the drama came from a book written two hundred years later! Still... maybe don't buy a flower for the price of a house. Follow for more!
